jobgether-jobgether:lever:2c2d2cea-c248-.title: Coder, Multispecialty
jobgether-jobgether:lever:2c2d2cea-c248-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Coder, Multispecialty based in the United States. This part-time role is responsible for accurate, compliant coding across a diverse range of medical specialties. You will review clinical documentation and translate diagnoses and procedures into precise CPT, ICD-10-CM, and HCPCS codes. Your work will directly support appropriate reimbursement, regulatory compliance, and the overall accuracy of the revenue cycle. The position offers exposure to specialties including family medicine, internal medicine, general surgery, and orthopedics. You will collaborate with physicians, healthcare professionals, billing teams, and revenue cycle specialists to resolve coding questions and denials. Strong attention to detail and a commitment to staying current with evolving coding standards will be essential to your success. The role is well suited to an experienced, certified coder who values accuracy, independence, teamwork, and continuous professional development. Assign accurate CPT, ICD-10-CM, and HCPCS codes to diagnoses and procedures for professional and facility services across multiple medical specialties. Review physician notes, operative reports, diagnostic reports, and other clinical documentation to identify all information required for accurate coding. Abstract relevant patient information from medical records for data entry, reporting, and statistical purposes. Identify unclear, incomplete, or inconsistent documentation and communicate with physicians and other healthcare providers to obtain clarification. Apply current coding guidelines, regulatory requirements, and payer-specific rules to ensure accurate and compliant coding. Participate in coding audits and contribute feedback and recommendations to improve coding quality and processes. Collaborate with billing and revenue cycle teams to investigate and resolve coding-related denials and claim rejections. Maintain strict patient confidentiality and comply with HIPAA privacy and security requirements. Keep coding knowledge current through continuing education, professional development, and monitoring of industry and regulatory changes. Provide guidance, training, and mentorship to less experienced coders when needed. Requirements: CPC or CCS certification required , with additional specialty certifications such as CEMC, CGSC, or COSC considered a plus. 3–5 years of multispecialty coding experience , preferably in a rural healthcare environment. Strong knowledge of CPT, ICD-10-CM, and HCPCS coding systems. Solid understanding of medical terminology, anatomy, and physiology. Thorough knowledge of Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payer coding guidelines and regulatory requirements. Experience working with electronic health record (EHR) systems and coding software. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities combined with exceptional attention to detail. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, particularly when working with physicians and other healthcare professionals. Ability to work independently while also collaborating effectively with a multidisciplinary team in a fast-paced environment. Commitment to continuous learning and staying current with coding updates, regulations, and industry best practices. Benefits: Work arrangement: Part-time position with a remote work environment. Opportunity to work across multiple medical specialties and gain broad clinical coding exposure. Collaborative environment with physicians, healthcare professionals, billing teams, and revenue cycle specialists. Opportunities to contribute to coding audits, process improvements, and quality initiatives. Professional development through ongoing education and exposure to evolving coding standards and regulations. Opportunity to mentor less experienced coding professionals and further develop leadership skills. Benefits and eligibility may vary based on empl

Provide technical guidance and knowledge sharing to team members while taking ownership of key deliverables and production issues. jobgether-jobgether:lever:6fffbe16-ccb8-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director of Finance based in Canada. This is a senior finance leadership opportunity for an experienced professional ready to oversee financial operations across multiple international entities. You will lead a distributed finance team while establishing scalable processes, strong controls, and consistent financial standards. The role combines technical accounting expertise with strategic planning, forecasting, reporting, and business partnership. You will work closely with the CFO and senior leadership to turn financial data into meaningful business insights and sound decisions. You will also drive improvements across finance systems, workflows, and automation as the organization grows. This role is well suited to a collaborative leader who thrives in an international, fast-paced, and evolving environment. Lead the finance function and manage an international team, including finance leads and their direct reports across multiple countries. Own hiring, development, performance management, succession planning, and team structure while fostering a high-performing and accountable finance culture. Oversee accounting operations end to end, including accounts payable, payments, reconciliations, and month-end and year-end close across multiple countries and currencies. Partner with the CFO and senior leadership on financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and analysis. Deliver accurate and timely financial information to leadership and, when required, the Board, providing insight and constructive challenge for commercial and strategic decisions. Serve as a trusted finance partner and senior escalation point for cross-border financial matters. Own finance systems, tools, and workflows, identifying opportunities for automation, efficiency, integration, and improved data reliability. Proven leadership experience managing managers or finance leads and building effective distributed or international teams. Strong knowledge of financial, tax, and regulatory requirements in Quebec or substantial experience operating within the Quebec market. Demonstrated experience managing finance operations across multiple countries, currencies, legal entities, and time zones. Strong technical finance and accounting judgment, combined with the ability to establish standards and scale processes effectively. Excellent communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to work confidently with the CFO, senior leadership, and teams across the organization. jobgether-jobgether:lever:8c0ae45a-d03d-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Finance Lead based in Canada. This is a high-ownership finance leadership opportunity within a lean, fast-moving technology environment. You’ll take responsibility for the day-to-day finance function while serving as a trusted strategic partner to senior leadership. The role combines FP&A, financial modeling, cash management, reporting, treasury, and operational finance. You’ll help leadership make informed decisions by providing accurate forecasts, actionable insights, and strong financial discipline. Working with a small internal team and external accounting, tax, and audit providers, you’ll have significant autonomy to shape how finance operates. The role is ideal for someone who thrives with responsibility, limited structure, and the opportunity to build efficient financial processes that support sustainable growth. Own the annual budgeting process, maintain operating forecasts and runway models, and provide financial analysis to support business planning and capital allocation. Develop business metrics, financial models, and performance reporting that give leadership clear and actionable visibility into company performance. Manage cash forecasting, liquidity planning, banking relationships, operational controls, and treasury-related activities. Monitor short- and long-term capital requirements and help ensure the organization maintains appropriate liquidity. Coordinate monthly and annual financial reporting, including board, investor, and management reporting packages. Oversee accounting close processes through external providers and ensure financial information is accurate and delivered on time. Manage relationships with external accounting, tax, audit, and other financial service providers, ensuring compliance obligations are completed efficiently. Oversee accounts payable and accounts receivable activities through the internal finance team. Maintain finance policies, procedures, and internal controls appropriate to the organization's size and stage. Support leadership with strategic and special projects, providing financial analysis and recommendations as required. Operate as a proactive finance partner to leadership, balancing financial discipline with the flexibility required in a high-growth environment. Build a finance function that operates efficiently, cost-effectively, and with minimal day-to-day oversight. Requirements 5+ years of relevant finance experience, with strong experience in FP&A, financial planning, and financial modeling. Proven experience working in startups, growth-stage companies, or venture-backed environments where ownership and adaptability are essential. Strong understanding of budgeting, forecasting, cash management, liquidity planning, and financial performance analysis. Experience managing external accounting, tax, audit, and other financial service providers. Ability to operate independently in a lean organization with limited structure and significant responsibility. Strong analytical and financial modeling capabilities, with the ability to turn complex financial information into practical business recommendations. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with confidence partnering with senior leadership and external stakeholders. High ownership mentality, strong attention to detail, and a bias toward action and problem-solving. Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution across day-to-day finance operations. Experience with treasury management is a plus. Experience in crypto, digital assets, or blockchain is a plus. Experience with legal entity restructuring, board reporting, investor reporting, or international organizations is advantageous. Benefits Highly competitive base salary of $185,000–$220,000 USD . Flexible and remote work environment. 25 days of annual holiday plus bank holidays . Opportunity to work at the cutting edge

southparkcommons-town:ashbyhq:0b261662-6.title: AI Product Engineer
southparkcommons-town:ashbyhq:0b261662-6.description: ABOUT TOWN Town is an AI-powered assistant that connects to your tools to do real work on your behalf -- triaging your inbox, drafting in your voice, managing your schedule, and running workflows across everything you use. It knows you deeply and gets sharper over time. ABOUT THE ROLE The core technical challenge at Town is: context from everywhere, action anywhere. The assistant pulls from your email, calendar, Slack, docs, and connected tools to build a deep understanding of who you are and what you need -- then executes reliably across all of them. Town is not a chat wrapper. It's a rethinking of email, calendar, and contacts through an AI-native lens, a workflow builder that lets anyone automate real work, a suggestion engine that discovers what to automate before you think to ask, and a network of assistants that talk to each other across teams and organizations. You'll design and ship the experiences that make all of that legible and loved. You'll be a foundational hire, working across the full stack but anchored on the product. You own features end to end -- from making tasteful UI/UX decisions to the backend plumbing that makes them real. Everyone has direct influence over product direction. The bar is high: the product has to feel polished, fast, and obviously better than the alternatives, on every surface. EXAMPLE PROJECTS INCLUDE... - Rethinking email, calendar, and contacts as AI-native experiences -- autonomous triage, drafts in your voice, 100% automated scheduling, an auto-built relationship graph - Building the suggestion engine -- tasks and workflow suggestions to inspire users on what to automate next - Designing the workflow builder -- making it trivial for anyone to build, share, and install automations - Building team and shared workflow surfaces -- one person builds, the whole team benefits - Building across web, desktop, mobile -- meeting users everywhere they work - Rethinking approvals, notifications, and the home screen -- the everyday surfaces that make or break trust in an agent YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU... - Are a generalist by choice -- comfortable moving between frontend, backend, and infrastructure as the problem demands. - Are excited about owning surface area end to end in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment -- not just executing within a defined spec. - Have strong product taste and can hold the whole experience in your head -- from the pixel to the prompt to the database schema. You care about how it feels, not just whether it works. - Have tuned your AI-native coding workflow that makes you dramatically faster and more effective. - Have experience with LLM-powered products, agentic UX, or any product where non-determinism is a first-class design constraint. - Have shipped product at a high-growth startup through an inflection point -- you were there when the product was being defined, not maintained. We want to hear your concrete shipping stories. - Care about trajectory over tenure. We're less interested in years of experience than how fast you got here and what you built along the way. - Are excited about working in-person, five days a week. We believe it matters at this stage. LOCATION 5 days per week in person in either SF or NYC.

strategichr-strategichr:greenhouse:78940.title: CNC Operator
strategichr-strategichr:greenhouse:78940.description: Job Opportunity: CNC Operator with Formative 3D in Falls Church, VA Do you enjoy working hands‑on with machines, tools, and materials to create high‑quality parts? Are you detail‑oriented and energized by technical craftsmanship in a fast‑paced manufacturing environment? Ready to support innovative production workflows using CNC machining and advanced 3D printing? If so, we’d love to meet you! Formative 3D is seeking a CNC Operator to support post‑processing operations and fabricate custom fixtures and jigs that enhance our production workflow. This role blends hands‑on machining with technical precision and close collaboration across production and engineering teams. You’ll operate CNC and robotic milling equipment to post‑process large‑format 3D‑printed furniture components while contributing to continuous improvements in efficiency, quality, and shop operations. Salary range: $28 - $33/hour Key Responsibilities You will work closely with production and engineering teams to: Operate 3‑axis CNC routers and 6‑axis robotic milling machines to post‑process 3D‑printed components and produce fixtures and jigs Interpret technical drawings and CAD files to set up and execute milling operations Perform post‑processing tasks on printed parts, including trimming, sanding, and surface finishing Inspect machined and printed parts for dimensional accuracy and quality standards Maintain, calibrate, and troubleshoot CNC equipment and tooling Collaborate with engineering and production teams to improve fixture design and workflow efficiency Assist with general shop duties, including material preparation, organization, and equipment upkeep What You Bring 2+ years of experience operating CNC milling machines in a production or prototyping environment Proficiency in reading technical drawings and using measurement tools such as calipers and micrometers Familiarity with G‑code, CAM software, and CNC setup procedures (Fusion 360 preferred) Strong mechanical aptitude and attention to detail Experience with post‑processing plastics or composite materials (preferred) Ability to work independently while contributing to a collaborative team environment Comfort lifting up to 50 lbs and working in a hands‑on shop setting Experience with 3D printing or furniture assembly—or a strong desire to learn—is a plus What We Offer: Compensation commensurate with experience Full suite of healthcare benefits, including medical, dental, and vision Competitive PTO plans Competitive retirement plans Why Join Formative 3D? Built environments can be manufactured the same way the best technology products are: faster, smarter and at scale. Formative 3D deploys full-scale manufacturing solutions built for speed, flexibility and real-world impact. By combining advanced 3D printing, robotics and technology, we rethink how physical products for the built world are created — from concept to installation. We design and manufacture products that range from high-end furniture systems and architectural lighting to jigs, fixtures, and tooling. Formative 3D pushes additive manufacturing forward and sets a new standard for how the built environment gets made. After years of research, our first production facility launched in 2026, and we’re already proving that a new model of manufacturing isn’t theoretical; it’s operational. Apply online today to join a great team! Formative 3D is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to hiring and developing the most qualified individuals based on job‑related experience, skills, and merit. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We value a respectful, inclusive workplace where everyone has the opportunity to succeed. Formative 3D maintains a drug‑free workplace consistent with applicable local, state, and federal laws. #ZR
